n merely abbreviates λ+1. Positivity and its interpretation as a dimension are not granted by the definition.
I is the finite integer interval [0,λ], even without a nonemptiness assumption. Nonemptiness and cardinality n are established separately under H001.
For i∈I the exponent and factorial have nonnegative integer arguments, so e_i=Y_i v is defined in V. Nonvanishing and the basis property remain N001.

H001 makes p a positive prime, so p∤b excludes b=0 and the allowed denominators form a multiplicative set. The specified fractions form the subring Z_(p) of Q, embedded in C; no map to K is assumed here.
The tensor product R⊗_Z M exists from the additive subgroup structure of M and the defined ring R. Freeness, rank and an embedding into V are left to N002.

The map (r,m)↦rm is Z-balanced and R-linear after tensoring, since R⊆C and M⊆V. Its image is exactly the R-span. The definition explicitly postpones identification with this image until injectivity is proved in N002.

H001 gives 0≤λ and thus 0∈I, so J=J_0 is legitimately defined. It does not assert the equality J_i=J or a nonzero generator.
M⊗_Z K has the standard K-vector-space structure using the integer-module structures of M and K. No nonzeroness or dimension is introduced as part of its definition.

H003 makes the Z-span of the standard generators closed under brackets, so its scalar extension defines a Lie algebra over K. The definition includes characteristic 2 and requires neither simplicity nor distinct reduced weights.
